QF.id: VB Concept and Role of Mutual Fund_21

question.text: What does an "exit load" in a mutual fund mean?

answer.text: A fee charged to investors when they redeem (sell) their units before a specified period
A fee charged when you buy mutual fund units
A penalty for investing too little money
The annual management fee charged by the fund

explanation.text: The Logic: An exit load reduces the redemption proceeds the investor receives. For example, if a 1% exit load applies, the investor receives 99% of the applicable NAV on repurchase. The Trap: Exit load is charged on exit (redemption), not on purchase. It is distinct from the annual TER and is not driven by the size of the investment. Note: Investors are also permitted to exit without an exit load when there is a change in the scheme's fundamental attributes, per the cited workbook page.
